title: Did Drew Mestemaker reestablish himself as a 2027 NFL Draft prospect vs. Oregon?
author: Dane Brugler
content:
Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker needed all of one play Saturday to start erasing his (and his team’s) disappointing Week 1 showing in a loss at Tulsa. Mestemaker broke loose for a 75-yard run on the Cowboys’ first offensive snap against Oregon, kickstarting a dazzling performance as he led Oklahoma State — a 24.5-point underdog — to a 39-31 upset of the No. 6 Ducks.

Mestemaker, who followed Oklahoma State coach Eric Morris from North Texas this offseason, finished with 317 yards and two touchdowns on 26-of-43 passing, plus added 109 yards and a touchdown rushing.

He did throw two interceptions, both on tipped balls, that led to 14 Oregon points in the first half. But he more than made up for it, ultimately sealing the victory with a 7-yard run for a first down with 1:33 left.

ESPN reported during the game’s broadcast that 20 NFL scouts, two general managers and one president of football operations were on hand at the game, presumably to see Oregon’s starting QB Dante Moore, a contender to be the No. 1 pick in April. However, Moore struggled to just 191 yards and two TDs on 14-of-29 passing behind an offensive line that had issues protecting him.

Mestemaker, on the other hand, likely elevated his own stock in just his second start at Oklahoma State.

It reaffirms that the preseason enthusiasm for Mestemaker’s NFL future was justified. After a disappointing debut last week, Mestemaker out-dueled Moore for most of the game and was the driving force behind a massive upset win.

The main takeaway: It is very, very easy to get excited about Mestemaker’s immense promise. The No. 4 QB for 2027 on my preseason draft board, he has outstanding arm talent, which he showed against Oregon both in terms of velocity to pierce keyhole windows and touch to layer the ball between coverages. He stays unbothered in the pocket to allow routes to develop and find his man. And his athleticism is a major asset. He executes at a high level on rollouts and boots and can stride out to take yardage with his legs.

Mestemaker had that 75-yard gain on the first-quarter run, picked up another 10 on a fourth-quarter touchdown that showed off his finishing toughness, and then kept it on a zone read to put the game away.

Most probably know the story by now, but Mestemaker didn’t start at quarterback in high school and was lucky to get a walk-on spot at North Texas before blowing up last year as a redshirt freshman. His inexperience is still evident in the way he predetermines throws and holds the ball too long, with inconsistent progression timing. But most of his issues are experience-based, so he should continue to improve them as he logs more snaps against top competition.

The physical traits are awesome, and Mestemaker plays with the competitiveness and unwavering confidence that directly leads to wins, as we saw on Saturday.

Considering his background (and that relative lack of experience), will he ultimately be better off going back to school next season instead of entering the 2027 NFL Draft? Probably, but that is a question we will continue to revisit throughout the year.
